2609.15609.title: Diversified and Perceptible Counterfactual Examples Leveraging Expert Knowledge
2609.15609.paper_summary: CounterFactual Examples (CFEs) are a cornerstone of eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), offering local, post hoc, and model-agnostic explanations by identifying minimal input modifications that alter a model's prediction. Yet, in order to be intelligible, these modifications must also be semantically meaningful to the explainee. This paper proposes to integrate knowledge expressed as a fuzzy linguistic vocabulary to represent the explainee's perception and interpretation of the data. The domain induced by this fuzzy vocabulary imposes structural constraints that make the features dependent, preventing the use of gradient-based optimisation methods for CFE generation, e.g., DiCE. The paper proposes a continuous data embedding in this linguistic domain and exploits it to define a variant of DiCE that allows personalisation for the explainee, named DiCEf. As illustrated by experimental results on a real-world dataset, this extension of the DiCE method enables the generation of CFEs that are linguistically perceptible while preserving cost minimality, sparsity, and diversity.
2609.15609.paper_summary_zh: 反事實範例（CFEs）是可解釋人工智慧（XAI）的基石，通過識別最小的輸入修改來改變模型的預測，提供局部的、事後的和模型無關的解釋。然而，為了使這些修改易於理解，它們必須對解釋對象在語義上也是有意義的。本文提出將知識以模糊語言詞彙的形式整合，以表示解釋對象對數據的感知和詮釋。這種模糊詞彙所引發的領域施加了結構約束，使特徵之間相互依賴，從而阻止了基於梯度的優化方法用於CFE生成，例如DiCE。本文提出在這個語言領域中進行連續數據嵌入，並利用它來定義一種DiCE的變體，允許針對解釋對象的個性化，稱為DiCEf。正如在真實世界數據集上的實驗結果所示，這一DiCE方法的擴展使得生成的CFEs在語言上可感知，同時保持成本最小化、稀疏性和多樣性。
